channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Alemanha contribuirá com 500 milhões de euros para Fundo Clima, diz Lula
item.description: Germany will contribute 500 million euros to the Climate Fund, administered by BNDES, as announced by President Lula during a press conference with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The amount, equivalent to approximately US$588.3 million, aims to support climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts in Brazil.

item.title: BNDES capta R$ 4,1 bi com Alemanha e instituições europeias para Fundo Clima e outros projetos verdes no Brasil
item.description: BNDES raised R$ 4.1 billion (700 million euros) from Germany's KfW, France's AFD, Italy's CDP, and the Inter-American Development Bank to finance Brazil's Climate Fund and sustainable mobility projects. Of this, R$ 3 billion goes to the National Climate Change Fund and R$ 1.1 billion to mobility initiatives, marking Germany's first contribution to the fund established in 2009. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of Hannover Messe, strengthens Brazil-Germany cooperation on ecological transition, focusing on renewable energy, reforestation, and emissions reduction.

item.title: Na Alemanha, Lula defende biodiesel contra restrições da UE
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended Brazil’s biodiesel production during a visit to Germany, criticizing ideological barriers in the European Union that threaten to reclassify soy-based biodiesel as non-renewable after 2030. Lula argued that Brazilian biofuel does not compromise food production or native forests and invited Europeans to visit Brazil to dispel myths about the sector.

item.title: Caso do Banco Master escancara jogo político e reforça imagem do mar de lama
item.description: The Banco Master case reveals an ongoing cycle of political crises in Brazil since 2013, with Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) attempting to indict STF ministers and the PGR for obstructing the investigation, though the CPI rejected his report. The episode reinforces the perception of a 'sea of mud' in Brazilian politics, deepening voter distrust amid rising polarization ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: O fator que pressiona Lula e é considerado por analistas a ameaça central à reeleição
item.description: The surge in food prices, particularly milk and meat, has become a central challenge for Lula's re-election bid, directly affecting inflation perception among voters earning two to five minimum wages. Analysts say this perception reinforces frustration over unfulfilled promises and is difficult to reverse in the short term due to international pressures and limited time. The government may resort to fiscal stimulus, but that risks exacerbating inflationary pressures.

item.title: A aposta de relator da PEC do fim da escala 6×1 sobre votação na CCJ
item.description: The rapporteur of the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale, Deputy Paulo Azi, stated he believes the report will be approved in the Chamber's CCJ without major difficulties, despite a view request from opposition lawmakers last week. The committee is set to review the matter this Wednesday, and if it advances, the text will proceed to a special committee before reaching the plenary. Chamber President Hugo Motta aims to complete all stages by the end of May, aligned with President Lula's agenda.

item.title: Celina Leão diz que Flávio Bolsonaro devia pedir perdão a Michelle
item.description: The governor of the Federal District, Celina Leão (PL-DF), said Senator Flávio Bolsonaro should apologize to former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro after their public exchanges of criticism, stating that reconciliation must come from him. She emphasized Michelle is a personal friend and political ally, and criticized Flávio’s approach of using social media to attack rather than engage in dialogue. Despite the tensions, Celina believes a family reconciliation is possible due to their shared political alignment.

item.title: Brasil pode ser parceiro da Alemanha em minerais críticos e biocombustíveis, avalia CNI
item.description: CNI President Ricardo Alban states Brazil has strong potential to become a major partner of Germany in biofuels and critical minerals, but progress depends on correcting European misconceptions about the environmental impact of Brazilian biofuel production. He emphasized the need to process and add value to natural resources, citing the Mercosul-European Union agreement as a driver to double bilateral trade with Germany from $20 billion to $40 billion within five years.

item.title: Quando é o próximo feriado? Confira a lista das próximas folgas de 2026
item.description: The article lists Brazil's 2026 holidays, noting that after Tiradentes' Day, upcoming days off include Labor Day (May 1), Corpus Christi (June 4), Independence Day (September 7), Our Lady of Aparecida (October 12), All Souls' Day (November 2), Republic Proclamation (November 15), Black Consciousness Day (November 20), and Christmas (December 25). It also highlights that states and municipalities may add local holidays, such as Saint George's Day in Rio de Janeiro (April 23), which, falling on a Thursday, could create extended breaks depending on local labor agreements.

item.title: Lula confunde Obama com Trump ao dizer que esperava Nobel da Paz em 2010
item.description: President Lula stated in Hannover that he expected to be nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize by Barack Obama after mediating the 2010 Tehran Agreement, initially confusing Obama with Donald Trump before correcting himself. He said he received the proposal handwritten from Obama and convinced Ahmadinejad to sign, but the U.S. increased sanctions on Iran instead of supporting the deal. Lula used the episode to criticize the lack of UN Security Council reform and denied Iran is developing nuclear weapons, likening it to the false pretext for the 2003 Iraq invasion.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest expõe um dado decisivo sobre a disputa Lula x Flávio
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula leading with 37% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 32% in the first round, and a technical tie in the second round (42% to 40% for the senator). However, 68% of voters have not yet declared a spontaneous vote, and over 40% say they could change their choice, indicating high volatility and low vote consolidation.

item.title: Brasil vive crise de representatividade que remete a 2012, diz fundador do RenovaBR
item.description: Eduardo Mufarej, founder of RenovaBR, warns Brazil is facing a new representativity crisis akin to the 2012–2016 period, marked by electoral distrust and citizens feeling unrepresented by political leaders. The crisis is exacerbated by Lula-Bolsonaro polarization, which has sidelined centrist candidates and discouraged new political entrants, alongside growing concerns about perceived corruption in the judiciary.

item.title: Lula: Brasil pode se transformar em uma Arábia Saudita dos combustíveis renováveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated at Hannover Messe 2026 in Germany for Brazil’s potential to become a global leader in renewable fuels, likening it to a 'Saudi Arabia of renewable fuels'. He argued that Brazil can produce biodiesel and ethanol without jeopardizing food production or forest areas, countering European claims that such biofuels threaten food security. Lula stressed the need to overcome EU trade barriers and emphasized the importance of decarbonizing transport through proven technologies.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Gilmar vai para cima de Romeu Zema
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes requested the inclusion of former governor Romeu Zema (Novo) in the fake news inquiry, heightening tensions between the judiciary and executive branches. The Meio-Dia em Brasília program also noted senators' push for a vote on the final report of the fake news CPI, suggesting potential acceleration of the legislative process.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cogita vereadora mais votada do Nordeste como vice
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is considering Fortaleza councilwoman Priscila Costa of the PL as a potential running mate for his 2026 presidential bid, aiming to strengthen support in the Northeast, a region historically favorable to the PT. Priscila Costa, president of PL Women in Ceará and a Senate pre-candidate, has met with Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro and is seen as capable of appealing to female and northeastern voters. The move comes amid declining PT popularity in the region due to inflation and reduced purchasing power.

item.title: Na Alemanha, Lula nega turbulência em cenário eleitoral e diz estar 'tranquilo' para disputar quarto mandato
item.description: President Lula stated he is calm about running for a fourth term, denying electoral turbulence and defending democracy and national self-determination. He also criticized U.S. interventions in Venezuela and Cuba, calling for respect for territorial integrity and the UN Charter. The Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) technically leading with 42% against Lula’s 40% in a potential 2026 runoff.

item.title: O mapa partidário de 2026
item.description: The 2026 party window confirmed a consolidated trend in Brazilian politics: under pressure from the electoral threshold, major parties strengthened their position, while smaller parties turned to federations, mergers, and incorporations as adaptation strategies. More than a mere reshuffling of candidacies, the period reflected a structural reorganization of the party system. This dynamic reinforces the concentration of power in a few dominant parties.

item.title: Em visita à Alemanha, Lula lembra 7 a 1 na Copa do Brasil e diz esperar 'que isso não se repita' este ano
item.description: During an official visit to Germany to open the Brazil Pavilion at Hannover Messe 2026, President Lula made a lighthearted comment recalling Brazil’s historic 7–1 loss to Germany in the 2014 World Cup, expressing hope that such a defeat would not be repeated this year. He noted Brazil avoids Germany in the group stage, being in Group C with Morocco, Haiti, and Scotland, while Germany is in Group E. The remarks were made at the 42nd Brazil-Germany Economic Meeting, held alongside the Hannover Messe, where Lula also advanced Brazil’s reindustrialization agenda and strategic partnerships in technology, energy, and innovation.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil não aceita ser ‘terceiro mundo’
item.description: President Lula stated at Hannover Messe in Germany that Brazil no longer accepts being labeled a 'third world' country and seeks recognition as a Global South nation with technological and economic capacity. He emphasized Brazil's economic stability, international credibility, and companies like Petrobras and Embraer as evidence of its potential for productive alliances with Europe.

item.title: Chanceler alemão defende ratificação de acordo entre União Europeia e Mercosul 'o mais rápido possível'
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for the 'as quick as possible' ratification of the EU-Mercosul agreement, calling Brazil an important and reliable partner in an increasingly complex world. He stated the deal would bring economic growth to both sides of the Atlantic and that Germany-Brazil trade could double from its current $20 billion annual volume. The agreement, negotiated for over 25 years, enters into force provisionally on May 1, pending final ratification by the EU and the European Parliament.

item.title: O Paradoxo da Mobilidade: o filho da faxineira ganhou diploma, não achou emprego e está frustrado com Lula
item.description: The article discusses the frustration of a young public university graduate, son of a cleaner, who despite earning a diploma cannot find work and blames the Lula government for lack of opportunity. This narrative illustrates the 'mobility paradox': upward social mobility through education fails to translate into economic inclusion, leading to disillusionment among voters who once supported the government.

item.title: Gilmar pede a inclusão de Zema no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes has requested the inclusion of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema in the fake news investigation after Zema posted a video with puppets implying Mendes would rule favorably for Justice Dias Toffoli in exchange for a stay at the Tayayá resort, previously owned by Toffoli’s family. The request was sent to Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the rapporteur of the inquiry, and prompted a response from Zema’s party, Novo, which defended the video as satire and accused the STF of being 'untouchable'.

item.title: Na Alemanha, Lula defende pioneirismo de biocombustíveis brasileiros
item.description: President Lula defended Brazil’s pioneering role in biofuels during a visit to Germany, emphasizing that sugarcane ethanol produces more energy per hectare and reduces emissions by up to 90% compared to gasoline. He criticized the EU’s environmental regulation for ignoring Brazil’s sustainable land-use practices and for applying a unilateral carbon calculation mechanism that overlooks the low emissions of Brazil’s renewable-based production process. Lula stated Brazil already achieved 50% renewable energy in its matrix by 2025 — well ahead of the EU’s 2050 target — and invited investors to bet on Brazil’s clean energy future.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede a Moraes a inclusão de Romeu Zema no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes sent a crime report to fellow Justice Alexandre de Moraes, requesting that former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema be investigated in the fake news inquiry. The report is based on a video Zema shared in March, using puppets and deep fake technology to simulate a conversation between Justices Dias Toffoli and Gilmar Mendes, alleging corruption and damaging the Court’s image. Zema has also previously called for the arrest of Moraes and Toffoli and said he would support Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential 2026 runoff.

item.title: Lula: 'Alemães não podem acreditar no mito de que o biocombustível atrapalha a produção de alimentos. Ninguém come biodiesel'
item.description: Lula criticized European barriers to Brazilian biofuels, rejecting the myth that they compete with food production and emphasizing food security as the world's greatest weapon. He also denounced unilateral EU carbon calculation mechanisms that ignore Brazil’s sustainable production practices and urged supporters of the EU-Mercosul agreement to speak louder than its critics.

item.title: LIVE - LULA FORA AGORA!! ADEUS PARA O PETISTA - BOLSONARO AVISOU!!
item.description: The video is a sensationalist live stream with a title demanding Lula's immediate removal from office, using aggressive language and a confrontational political tone. It lacks substantive arguments, focusing only on slogans like 'BOLSONARO AVISOU!!' and repeating protest phrases against the petista. There is no discussion of public policies or electoral proposals.

item.title: PT ataca Flávio Bolsonaro nas redes usando impulsionamento de conteúdos negativos, que antes rejeitava
item.description: The PT is boosting negative content against Flávio Bolsonaro on social media, adopting a strategy it previously rejected. This tactical shift reflects a more aggressive political approach aimed at damaging the senator’s image. The article notes that the party now uses virtual guerrilla tools to attack opponents, despite having criticized such methods in the past.

item.title: MORAES RESPONDE A FLAVIO BOLSONARO: QUER DESEQUILIBRAR AS ELEIÇÕES DE 2026! LULA MOSTRA FORÇA REAL!
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes responded to accusations from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, claiming he seeks to destabilize the 2026 elections by spreading disinformation. President Lula was highlighted as demonstrating real strength in governing the country, in contrast to opposition claims. The excerpt suggests an atmosphere of institutional tension between state powers and allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Artigo: Transição sob tensão: Constituição, neutralidade e reconstrução no Rio
item.description: Rio de Janeiro is experiencing an institutional crisis following the TSE’s removal of the governor and the Alerj president for serious electoral offenses, combined with the vice-governor’s resignation, breaking the democratic legitimacy chain. The article argues that, according to the state constitution and the timing of the vacancy, the president of the Tribunal of Justice should assume executive leadership, as institutional neutrality is crucial to prevent political capture and ensure stability during the transition. Judicial interim leadership — not parliamentary — is presented as a tool for democratic reconstruction amid institutional decay and organized crime influence.

item.title: PT morde STF após Lula soltar mão do 'companheiro' Moraes
item.description: The Workers' Party publicly criticized the Supreme Federal Court after President Lula reduced his support for Justice Alexandre de Moraes. The shift comes amid the Master case, which overburdened the decision-making processes of the government and the party. The PT now includes in its agenda the demand for stricter ethical standards for the STF.

item.title: Em Hannover, Lula defende imigração diante de chanceler alemão criticado por declarações
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended immigration during a speech at the Hannover Industrial Fair in Germany, alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who has previously faced criticism for anti-immigration statements. Lula emphasized immigration as a key issue in European and global elections, countering restrictive narratives.

item.title: Lula na Alemanha: 'Brasil cansou de ser tratado como país pequeno ou invisível'
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil is tired of being treated as a small or invisible country, emphasizing the importance of the partnership with Germany and Europe during the opening of Hannover Messe. He praised the EU-Mercosul agreement, criticized false claims about Brazilian agriculture and biofuel barriers, and highlighted the historical Brazil-Germany relationship dating back to 1850. Lula also condemned the era of fake news, while the German chancellor praised Brazil's leadership in energy transition and agricultural technologies.

item.title: “Taxação do Pix é ideia do Bolsonaro”, diz Haddad
item.description: Former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (PT), a pre-candidate for governor of São Paulo, accused former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL) of being the originator of the Pix taxation idea. He also attempted to link President Lula (PT) to the extrajudicial liquidation of Banco Master, decreed by the Central Bank in November 2025.

item.title: O mundo não pode ser dirigido por mentiras, diz Lula na Alemanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attended the Hannover Messe in Germany, advocating for multilateralism and criticizing the spread of fake news, stating that 'the world cannot be led by lies'. He warned about the dangers of the digital revolution and disinformation, implicitly referencing authoritarian tendencies without naming Donald Trump. His schedule includes the Brazil-Germany economic meeting, high-level intergovernmental consultations, a visit to Wolfsburg, and concludes in Lisbon to discuss the new nationality law and bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Girão critica inclusão de Zema em inquérito das fake news
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) harshly criticized the potential inclusion of former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema in the Supreme Court's fake news inquiry, calling the move 'shameful'. He accused STF ministers of partisanship and using the inquiry to persecute political opponents. Girão argued that the inquiry is being weaponized for political persecution rather than combating disinformation.

item.title: O fator que divide bolsonaristas sobre a possível candidatura de Ciro Gomes à Presidência
item.description: Bolsonaristas are divided on the possibility of Ciro Gomes running for president: some see him as a strategic ally to strengthen opposition to the PT in the Northeast and benefit Flávio Bolsonaro in Ceará, even without direct support; others view him as a valuable adversary to generate presidential clashes against Lula in debates. The invitation came from Aécio Neves (PSDB-MG).

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 20 de abril
item.description: The JCaesar cartoon published on April 20, 2026, offers political humor about events in Brasília, involving the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) and current affairs. The illustration uses sarcasm to comment on recent government decisions, maintaining the artist's characteristic critical tone. It is part of VEJA's humor section, focusing on institutional satire.

item.title: Gilmar pede a Moraes para investigar Zema no inquérito das fake news por vídeo com sátira ao STF
item.description: Minister Gilmar Mendes requested that Minister Alexandre de Moraes investigate former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema for sharing a satirical video targeting the STF, which Mendes claims harms the Court’s honor and his personal reputation. The video, featuring puppets resembling Toffoli and Mendes, references a real decision by Mendes that annulled secrecy breaks in Toffoli’s company. Zema, who left office to run for president, has intensified criticism of the STF, proposing a new Supreme Court if elected.

item.title: Produção de biocombustíveis não impacta produção alimentar, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated that biofuel production in Brazil does not impact food production, rejecting the European criticism based on the ILUC concept. He emphasized that Brazil has over 40 million hectares of degraded land that can be restored to produce both food and biofuels without encroaching on native vegetation. Lula dismissed European concerns as a 'mythology' and asserted that no one would replace food production with biofuels.

item.title: Lula volta a defender biocombustíveis ao abrir Feira de Hannover e reclama de regulação europeia
item.description: Lula defended Brazilian biofuels at the Hannover Industrial Fair, arguing that food should not be replaced by fuel. He criticized European regulations that, he claims, hinder Brazilian biodiesel exports. Brazil is the guest country at the 79th edition of the event.

item.title: Lula defende agro e pede para alemães não crerem em 'mitos' sobre biocombustíveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended Brazilian agribusiness during an event in Brasília, emphasizing the sector's importance to the national economy. He urged Germans not to believe 'myths' about biofuel production, stating that Brazil produces sustainably and efficiently. Lula stressed the need for international cooperation based on facts, not prejudice.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes aciona Zema no inquérito das Fake News, após vídeo postado nas redes
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes filed a criminal complaint against former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, a Novo party presidential candidate, after Zema shared an AI-generated deepfake video depicting Mendes in a fictitious conversation with Dias Toffoli about the Banco Master scandal. Mendes claims the video harms his reputation and that of the Court, requesting investigation under the fake news inquiry. Reporter Alexandre de Moraes forwarded the case to the PGR, and the process remains under seal.

item.title: Lula cita 7 a 1 ao abrir discurso na Alemanha: “Que não se repita”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva referenced Brazil's 7-1 loss to Germany in the 2014 World Cup while opening the Brazil-Germany Economic Meeting in Hannover, expressing hope that such a result would not be repeated in the 2026 World Cup. He urged private sector support to convert the provisional EU-Mercosul agreement into a permanent pact, calling it an essential instrument for the economies of Europe and South America.

item.title: Lula pede engajamento da Europa para vigência do acordo Mercosul-UE
item.description: President Lula called for European and private sector engagement to turn the provisional validity of the Mercosul-EU trade agreement into permanent, noting it enters into force on May 1. He emphasized the deal as essential for improving Brazilian trade and delivering benefits to workers, businesses, and consumers amid a turbulent global environment.

item.title: Visita à Alemanha prova que a sustentabilidade é arma da diplomacia econômica
item.description: President Lula visited Hannover Messe in Germany to defend the sustainability of Brazilian agriculture and criticize barriers to biofuels, highlighting the country's clean energy matrix as a strategy to improve Brazil's international image and expand business amid the oil crisis and the imminent entry into force of the Mercosul-European Union agreement. He was backed by business leaders and politicians who see the environmental agenda as an opportunity for economic diplomacy.

item.title: Na Alemanha, Lula defende biocombustíveis brasileiros e critica regras ambientais da União Europeia
item.description: Lula defended Brazilian biofuels in Germany, emphasizing their low CO₂ emissions and Brazil’s potential to lead the global energy transition. He criticized EU environmental regulations for overlooking Brazil’s sustainable practices, such as renewable energy use in ethanol and biodiesel production, warning that these rules could hinder clean energy access for European consumers despite Brazil’s proven efficiency.

item.title: Marinha prevê R$ 1,4 milhão em transporte a militares nas eleições
item.description: The Brazilian Navy estimates spending R$ 1.4 million on river transport of military personnel using small boats called 'voadeiras' during the 2026 elections in the Amazon region. The boats, contracted in 32 lots, will move troops from the 5th Jungle Infantry Battalion to remote riverside communities as part of the Voting and Counting Guarantee Operation (GVA). The vessels must carry up to 12 passengers and 1.2 tons of cargo, with safety equipment and navigation capability in narrow waterways.

item.title: Gilmar quer Zema no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Justice Gilmar Mendes requested, via a crime-report, that fellow Justice Alexandre de Moraes include former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) in the fake news investigation. The request was forwarded to the Attorney General's Office and remains confidential, as is customary. The information was reported by Folha de S.Paulo and reposted by O Antagonista.

item.title: Título de eleitor: prazo para tirar ou regularizar vai até 6 de maio
item.description: Voters have until May 6, 2025, to obtain, update, or regularize their voter registration, or risk being unable to vote in the 2026 elections, with the first round scheduled for October 4. The process can be completed in person at electoral courts or Justice Electoral posts, or online via the TSE’s Self-Service Electoral Portal, though biometric collection requires an in-person visit. Required documents include a photo ID proving Brazilian nationality, a recent proof of residence, and, for men turning 19, proof of military service completion.

item.title: Gilmar pede a Moraes para incluir Zema em inquérito das Fake News
item.description: Minister Gilmar Mendes requested that former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema be included in the Fake News Inquiry, alleging that a video depicting Mendes and Justice Dias Toffoli as puppets with sophisticated editing vilifies the honor of the STF and serves personal promotion. The video, released last month, simulates dialogues between the two justices using puppet representations.
